DRC People Operations & Safety Associate (Fixed-Term) Seeking an exceptional People Operations professional with 3-5 years of experience to safeguard our DRC team by driving daily duty of care, managing incident response, and enforcing strict safety compliance across complex field operations. Location: Democratic Republic of the Congo Career Level: Professionals APPLY NOW About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. About the Role The DRC People Operations & Duty of Care Associate will drive the daily execution, administration, and continuous maintenance of health, safety, and duty of care systems for the DRC program. Acting as a crucial operational and staff-facing focal point, this role is responsible for ensuring compliance with staff safety and security protocols across offices, transport, accommodations, warehouses, and field operations in a complex environment. You will ensure that established standard operating procedures (SOPs), incident management processes, and people safety and security systems are practically implemented, clearly communicated, and consistently followed by all staff. This role has a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the option to renew on business terms. Responsibilities Duty of Care & Safety Administration Maintain and regularly update foundational risk profiles, movement protocols, and safety logs across all operational locations. Serve as the central administrative focal point for incident management, ensuring timely documentation, structured reporting, and tracking of corrective actions. Act as the budget administrator for staff well-being, safety, and security expenditures, ensuring resources are tracked and utilized efficiently. Oversee the day-to-day implementation and upkeep of established Health, Safety, and Security SOPs (including staff movement, office/warehouse safety, and emergency response). Ensure all policies and procedures are practically integrated into daily routines, clearly communicated, and consistently applied across all departments. Maintain organized physical and digital filing systems for all compliance, safety, and personnel records. Monitor local security developments, political events, and public health situations (e.g., protests, elections, regional conflicts, or health alerts) to proactively provide intelligence updates and advise on necessary operational adjustments. Training, Onboarding & Capacity Building Coordinate the logistics, scheduling, and tracking for staff well-being, duty of care, and basic safety training programs. Facilitate thorough administrative inductions for new staff, consultants, and visitors, ensuring they receive, understand, and acknowledge all safety protocols. Maintain accurate tracking systems to ensure 100% staff compliance with organizational training requirements. Incident Management & Support Serve as the first-line point of contact for staff reporting workplace incidents, accidents, or health events. Maintain up-to-date emergency contact trees, phone trees, and vendor lists to ensure rapid execution of crisis management plans when needed. Champion a culture of care, proactively encouraging staff to utilize available resources and reporting systems. Serve as the primary operational focal point and key contact for external health and security service providers. Cross-Functional Execution & Office Management Oversee day-to-day office management and facility administration, ensuring workspaces consistently meet foundational health, safety, and duty of care standards. Partner closely with HR, Operations, and Supply Chain to embed people-centric systems into broader operational planning. Manage administrative relationships with vendors related to office facilities, basic guarding, and staff health services. Proactively establish, maintain, and leverage positive working relationships with local authorities, emergency services, police, and traffic departments to ensure rapid support during incidents. Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: * Academic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Operations Management, Public Administration, Organizational Psychology, or a related field. * Professional Certifications (Optional but Advantageous): HR or administrative certifications (e.g., SHRM-CP, PHR, CIPD, or local equivalents). Project management or process improvement certifications (e.g., CAPM, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt). Basic safety or trauma-informed care certifications (e.g., Advanced First Aid, Mental Health First Aid). * Experience: 3–5 years of experience in HR administration, operations, office management, or duty of care, preferably within an NGO, humanitarian, or fast-paced operational context. * Systems Execution: Proven track record of implementing, maintaining, and enforcing organizational SOPs, policies, and administrative frameworks. * Process-Oriented: Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage documentation, track compliance, and administer budgets accurately. * People Skills: High emotional intelligence with the ability to act as a trusted "para-HR" figure; capable of championing staff safety while firmly ensuring policy compliance. * Crisis Competence: Calm under pressure, with the ability to follow established emergency protocols and manage the administrative logistics of incident response. * Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; fluency in English and French required. Preferred Start Date: As soon as possible Job Location: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo Benefits: Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits Contract Duration: 1 year Eligibility One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred. Application Deadline 17 January 2027 . Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made. One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @ oneacrefund.org address. Finance and Administration Director Job ID: 2026-8315 Location: CD-Kinshasa Category: Local Employment Status: Full-Time Overview Jhpiego seeks a Finance and Administration Director to provide financial and administrative management for the AFGHS-Jhpiego project, funded by the U.S. Department of State (DoS) to support Global Health Security activities in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The $6 million project aims to support stronger, more resilient health systems at all levels; save lives; decrease morbidity and disability; and increase the potential of women, newborns, children, families, and communities to thrive. The Director will provide financial and administrative management, overseeing all financial, contractual, information technology, human resources, and procurement aspects for the project. The Director will ensure that the financial reports are compatible with standard accounting practices and follow Jhpiego and U.S. DoS rules and regulations. Responsibilities Financial Management & Leadership Provide overall project leadership and oversight of project level financial and support administrative operations, including support for project start-up, closeout, and establishment of field offices as required. Develop, implement, and strengthen project-specific financial management strategies, SOPs, internal controls, and administrative procedures consistent with Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins University (JHU), and DoS policies and systems. Provide strategic financial advice, analysis, and guidance to the Country Director, Sr Finance Manager- Country Office, Project Director, and project management team to support effective implementation and management decision-making. Supervise, mentor, and strengthen the capacity of finance staff and promote consistent application of financial policies, systems, and controls across project locations. Proactively identify financial, operational, compliance, and fiduciary risks and work with leadership to develop and monitor appropriate mitigation measures. Financial Planning, Budgeting, & Milestone Management Lead development and management of annual project budget, work plan budget, projections, and budget revisions in collaboration with program, technical, and global AFGHS-Jhpiego team. Align project budgets, expenditures, forecasts, and resource allocations with approved work plans, project milestones, and payment-linked deliverables, proactively monitoring financial and implementation progress and addressing gaps that could affect timely achievement, verification, and payment of milestones. Monitor project level burn rates, expenditures, pipeline, commitments, and financial performance and provide timely analysis to support programmatic and management decision-making. Prepare financial projections and scenario analyses to ensure sufficient resources are available to achieve project priorities and approved milestones. Proactively manage annual funding cycles and ensure expenditures are appropriately planned, incurred, recorded, and reconciled within applicable funding periods. Establish and maintain financial tracking of payment-linked milestones, including milestone value, expected achievement and verification dates, payment status, and implications for project cash flow and financial projections. Work closely with the Project Director, technical leads, MERL, and operations teams to routinely review progress against payment-linked milestones, identify milestones at financial or implementation risk, and support timely corrective action. Alongside, the global AFGHS-Jhpiego team, coordinate the financial and administrative requirements for milestone verification, invoicing, and payment, ensuring required supporting documentation is complete, accurate, compliant, and submitted within required timelines. Financial System, Control, and Reporting Ensure accurate financial, contractual and administrative reporting of the project compliant with Jhpiego and DOS’s rules and regulations, and terms and conditions of the award Oversee day-to-day coordination of financial activities ensuring cost efficiency Maintain and administer an on-site financial accounting and bookkeeping system (QuickBooks) required to assure the integrity and effective performance of financial operations and prepare monthly reports Oversee project’s day-to-day cash needs, payments, procurement, contracts, sub-grants, reviewing/processing invoices, district office start-up, operation systems, policies and procedures, consultant payments Provide guidance to project team members regarding the financial requirements of the project and office operations in compliance with DOS, Johns Hopkins University, and Jhpiego procedures and policies Lead the development, monitoring, and review of project budgets; review monthly financial analysis and budget vs. expense reports to determine reasonableness of variances and take appropriate actions, as required Provide guidance, monitoring and support to project team, including procurement for goods and services, logistical support for local and international travel (including expense reports) for staff and consultants, contracts development and management and maintenance of office inventory Serve as a key financial liaison with DoS, Global AFGHS-Jhpiego, and other relevant stakeholders as required. Compliance, Risk Management, and Audit Readiness Ensure adherence to Jhpiego and JHU financial, personnel, administrative, procurement, and operational policies and procedures and compliance with applicable donor requirements and Democratic Republic of Congo laws and regulations. Ensure compliance with statutory requirements related to payroll, income tax, VAT, organizational registration, and other applicable regulatory obligations. Identify and communicate significant compliance, financial, and operational risks to appropriate country and Baltimore leadership and provide guidance to resolve identified issues. Facilitate the work of external audits and ensure that financial records are properly maintained and readily available during audits Direct and oversee the monitoring and annual auditing of cost-share requirements, tracking and reporting Mentor, support, supervise and manage a team of highly qualified staff and align their efforts in concert with project goals to ensure rapid and sustainable results Ensure that Jhpiego human resources and administrative procedures are in place for the project and staff are in compliance. These include timekeeping, tracking of leave, sick days, absence, personnel employment records, and other human resources actions Sub-Awards, Partnerships, and Financial Oversight Collaborate with the Grants Manager and the AFGHS-Jhpiego contracts person and relevant program and finance teams to review and administer project sub-agreements. Review and provide financial and compliance input into award documents, modifications, and other binding agreements issued to or by Jhpiego. Support appropriate selection, financial assessment, management, monitoring, and closeout of sub-recipients in accordance with Jhpiego and JHU policies and donor requirements. Strengthen financial management and accountability capacity of sub-recipients and local partners and ensure identified financial or compliance gaps are addressed. Ensure timely financial closeout of sub-awards and completion of all required final financial reporting. Required Qualifications Master’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance, Accounting or relevant field 10 years of finance and administrative experience At least eight years of experience with financial analysis, financial reporting, cash flow analysis, budget development and forecasting, preferably on USG funded international health projects At least eight years providing financial planning and management, human resources and procurement for projects in West Africa, preferably in DRC Experience hiring staff and previous direct supervisory experience of professional and support staff Knowledge of USG cost principles, including DOS regulations, GAAP accounting rules and grants contract management Demonstrated experience organizing resources and establishing priorities Subcontract or subagreement financial management experience Knowledge of financing mechanisms - contracts and grants and their relevant terms and conditions Experience developing and/or implementing finance and accounting policies, procedures and systems Excellent verbal, written, interpersonal, and presentation skills in English and French Excellent diplomacy skills and a proven ability to establish and maintain interpersonal and professional relationships with DOS, host-country counterparts and representatives from other key stakeholders such as NGOs, CSOs, and the private sector Excellent skills in facilitation, team building, and coordination Ability to coach, mentor and develop financial and administrative capacity of project staff In-depth knowledge of financial software applications, databases and spreadsheets, including QuickBooks Enterprise, and Microsoft Office Ability to travel nationally and internationally APPLY

description: OFFRE D’EMPLOI Consultant(e) en Logistique pour la clôture du Projet POSTE : Consultant(e) en Logistique pour la clôture du Projet LIEU DU POSTE : Kinshasa SUPERVIS EUR: Operations and Logistic Specialist PROJET : Global Health Supply Chain – Procurement and Supply Management (GHSC-PSM), Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) DUREE : 4 mois Contexte : Le projet GHSC-PSM a comme objectif principal d'assurer un approvisionnement ininterrompu en produits de santé publique qui sauvent des vies dans le monde entier. Ce projet améliore la prestation des soins de santé grâce à des solutions de chaîne d'approvisionnement transformatrices, en se concentrant sur quelques domaines clés de la santé : le VIH/SIDA, le paludisme, la santé maternelle et infantile, la nutrition et les menaces émergentes pour la santé publique et représente un mécanisme par lequel le DOS offre une assistance technique mondiale pour les produits de santé. Remplir tous les formulaires de cession d’équipements pour chaque bénéficiaire Organiser et superviser la destruction des biens non fonctionnels, irréparables ou obsolètes ; Assurer la documentation complète des opérations réalisées ; Produire les rapports et dossiers justificatifs requis pour l'audit de clôture. description: OFFRE D’EMPLOI POSTE : CONSULTANT SPECIALISTE DU CLOSEOUT (CLOTURE du projet) Supervision : DIRECTRICE DES FINANCES ET OPERATIONS Lieu : K inshasa Type contrat : CONSULTANCE Durée : 60 jours ouvrables Le projet GHSC-PSM a comme objectif principal d'assurer un approvisionnement ininterrompu en produits de santé publique qui sauvent des vies dans le monde entier. Ce projet améliore la prestation des soins de santé grâce à des solutions de chaîne d'approvisionnement transformatrices, en se concentrant sur cinq domaines clés de la santé : le VIH/SIDA, le paludisme, la planification familiale volontaire et la santé reproductive, la santé maternelle et infantile, et les menaces émergentes pour la santé publique et représente un mécanisme par lequel le DOS offre une assistance technique mondiale pour les produits de santé dans les domaines suivants : Renforcer les systèmes d'approvisionnement nationaux, et Collaboration stratégique pour améliorer la disponibilité à long terme des produits de santé. L'objectif du présent cahier des charges est d'accompagner le processus de clôture du projet GHSC-PSM, dont la clôture est prévue pour le 30 juin 2027. Responsibilities include: Soutenir les activités de clôture du projet, en assurant une liaison régulière avec le personnel sur le terrain et l’équipe de gestion du projet (PST) du siège, et en veillant au respect total des réglementations et normes de l’USG. Aider l ’équipe de gestion de projet à répondre aux exigences techniques, administratives et contractuelles, en accordant une attention particulière à une clôture conforme et dans les délais. Assurer la sauvegarde des données et des rapports de l’ensemble du projet dans des référentiels locaux et en ligne appropriés, et effectuer un suivi auprès du personnel responsable pour garantir la conformité. Surveiller et mettre à jour le tableau de suivi de la clôture, tenir régulièrement informés l’unité de gestion de projet (PST) et l’ensemble du personnel du projet de l’avancement des travaux, et signaler sans délai tout sujet de préoccupation qui pourrait survenir. Soutenir l’équipe locale, selon les besoins, dans le cadre du départ et de la transition du personnel du projet, conformément à la législation locale du travail et aux réglementations de USG. Apporter son soutien à la cession de tous les biens figurant dans l’inventaire du projet GHSC-PSM et veiller à ce que les documents appropriés soient remplis et archivés avant la clôture. Vérifier les dossiers du projet pour s’assurer qu’ils sont complets et correctement enregistrés ; collaborer avec le bureau du projet pour combler les éventuelles lacunes. Aider l'équipe de gestion de projet à répondre aux exigences techniques, administratives et contractuelles, en veillant tout particulièrement à ce que la clôture du projet se fasse dans le respect des règles et dans les délais impartis. Veiller au respect des réglementations de l’USG, des politiques d’entreprise de Chemonics et de la législation congolaise. Mettre en place des normes et des procédures visant à garantir l’efficacité et l’efficience des programmes de conformité tout au long du projet. Veiller au classement adéquat et à l’organisation générale des documents administratifs. Effectuer toute tâche supplémentaire demandée par le chef de projet et/ou son représentant. Qualifications: Un master en administration des affaires, en finance, en comptabilité ou dans toute autre discipline pertinente est souhaité. Solides compétences en matière de leadership, d’accompagnement, de gestion, de planification, d’analyse et d’organisation, démontrées par la capacité à travailler aussi bien de manière autonome qu’en équipe, à évaluer les priorités et à gérer diverses activités avec le souci du détail.
